sentences.text: Fossils of Kimmerosaurus have been found in England and Norway.
Much of the description of Kimmerosaurus is based on its teeth, which are recurved and compressed from cheek to tongue side.
The premaxilla of Kimmerosaurus has eight teeth, while each ramus of the jaw has thirty-six teeth.
The skull of Kimmerosaurus is similar to Cryptoclidus but is much broader.
Peter Langham discovered the holotype and a second specimen at Endcome Bay, Dorset, in 1976, leading to the species name Kimmerosaurus langhami.
A more complete specimen (EC K2134) was discovered in the Etches Collection in 2015 and assigned to Kimmerosaurus by Roberts et al. in 2025.
The holotype of Kimmerosaurus is a partial skull (NHMUK R.8431) that was previously classified as Cryptoclidus eurymerus.
Two additional specimens were assigned to Kimmerosaurus in 1986: one found by Peter Langham in 1976 and another found by R. Damon in Weymouth around 1884.
Three potential Kimmerosaurus specimens, mostly postcranial, were excavated in Svalbard between 1994 and 2009.
Kimmerosaurus is classified as the sister taxon of Cryptoclidus within the family Cryptoclididae.
Kimmerosaurus fossils are found in the Kimmeridge Clay Formation near Kimmeridge, Dorset, England.
Kimmerosaurus likely ranged across much of the modern-day Jurassic Coast in southern England.
Kimmerosaurus lived during the Kimmeridgian to Tithonian stages, from 154.8 to 145.06 million years ago.
Researchers have debated whether Kimmerosaurus fossils might actually represent the missing skull of the similar plesiosaur Colymbosaurus due to a lack of post-cranial remains.
